page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The host system utilizes an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The VM is provisioned with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated virtual CPUs through simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 256.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU cache configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache.

The server package integrates 1288 GB of local SSD storage for fast temporary scratch space, swap partitions, and caching tiers. No discrete GPU acceleration is included. Hardware instruction capabilities include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA support, along with AMD SVM virtualization flags.

Benchmark testing highlights strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording a score of 2703.79, placing it in the top 25th percentile. Multi-threaded processing reaches a stress-ng score of 21625.7 and a PassMark CPU rating of 21615.24. In memory benchmarks, the system demonstrated 43.86 GB/s large-block read throughput, 26.01 GB/s large-block write throughput, and achieved 16.04 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

The constrained-core layout of the E32-16ads_v5 delivers memory and storage capacity typical of a 32-vCPU chassis while exposing only 16 vCPUs. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for database management systems and commercial software packages licensed strictly on a per-core basis, maximizing available RAM without paying for unused CPU licenses. A natural tradeoff is reduced aggregate compute parallelism relative to fully unconstrained 32-core variants.

This instance configuration is targeted at memory-heavy workloads, including enterprise relational database engines such as SQL Server and PostgreSQL, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis caching layers, and memory-bound batch analytics pipelines.

It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 256.0 GB of memory, and 1288 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage, operating without discrete GPU hardware. The platform displays strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng evaluations, alongside reliable multi-core throughput and high-capacity memory bandwidth capable of sustaining 16.04 million Redis SET operations per second. Configured as a constrained-core instance, it offers 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, enabling notable qualitative cost advantages for software stacks licensed by core count. The E32-16ads_v5 is engineered for memory-bound enterprise software, relational database management systems, caching clusters, and analytical data workloads requiring substantial memory density and local temporary disk performance.
